name: @projexlight/hdk-map
summary: Hardware-driven map kit: per-tenant tile-provider routing (Mapbox / Google / Apple / ESRI / OSM-self-host), capability negotiation (turn-by-turn, isochrone, offline tiles), and a thin server-side API for the mobile + web clients to fetch the right configuration at runtime. Keeps tile-provider keys on the server so mobile binaries don't ship credentials.

endpoints.description: Return the active provider's capability matrix (turn-by-turn? offline? isochrone? max-zoom?).
Return the per-tenant configured providers + the active one, with rotation-safe public keys.

events.name: hdk-map.provider.switched.v1
events.description: Operator switched the active tile provider (cost / outage / regional compliance).

events.name: hdk-map.tiles.quota.warn.v1
events.description: Provider quota nearing limit; ops should provision / switch before throttling kicks in.

hooks.name: getCapabilities
hooks.description: Return active provider's capability matrix for a tenant + region.

hooks.name: getTileProviders
hooks.description: List configured providers + active one. Returns rotation-safe public keys; private keys stay vault-wrapped.

hooks.name: switchProvider
hooks.description: Operator-driven switch with a reason. Audited; emits .provider.switched.v1.

scenarios.title: Tech mobile app boots → fetches provider capabilities
scenarios.when_to_use: App startup. Client doesn't hardcode provider; calls /api/hdk/map/capabilities + builds the UI for whatever the tenant is on today.
scenarios.expected_outcome: Returns { provider: 'mapbox-v11', offline_tiles: true, turn_by_turn: true, max_zoom: 22, isochrone: true }. App configures features accordingly.

scenarios.title: Operator switches from Google to Mapbox after pricing change
scenarios.when_to_use: Google bumped per-request pricing; operator switches to a cheaper provider with similar capabilities. Audited for the cost-justification trail.
scenarios.expected_outcome: Provider switched atomically; emits .provider.switched.v1 with operator + reason. Mobile clients pick up the new provider on next /api/hdk/map/capabilities poll.

scenarios.title: Tile quota warning fires before throttling kicks in
scenarios.when_to_use: Provider reports 80% of monthly quota consumed; we want ops to provision more or switch providers before customers see throttling.
scenarios.expected_outcome: Event fires; sdk-notification routes to oncall via Slack + PagerDuty. Ops has time to provision additional quota or switch providers before customers experience map degradation.

scenarios.title: EU-data-residency tenant pinned to ESRI EU + OSM Europe
scenarios.when_to_use: Tenant compliance profile requires EU-resident map tiles. Provider config pinned to EU-region endpoints + audited annually.
scenarios.example_code:
// config in db, surfaced via /api/hdk/map/tile-providers:
{ active: 'esri-eu', providers: [{ name: 'esri-eu', region: 'eu-west-1', residency: 'EU' }, ...] }
scenarios.expected_outcome: Mobile + web clients always hit EU endpoints for this tenant. switchProvider attempts to a non-EU provider refuse with a policy error pointing at the residency profile.

scenarios.title: Tech prefetches offline tiles for an upcoming rural route
scenarios.when_to_use: Route includes areas with poor cell signal; tech prefetches tiles before driving out. Capability negotiation tells the app this provider supports offline.
scenarios.expected_outcome: Tiles cached locally before the tech leaves cell range. Tile counts billed via the provider, not by ProjexCloud — but we cap per-tech offline volume to avoid runaway downloads.

compliance_posture.notes: Tile-provider keys stay vault-wrapped — public ('discoverable') keys are rotation-safe scoped tokens, never the master account credential. EU tenants pinned to EU-region providers; switchProvider enforces residency profile. Map fetch metadata is location data — FCC §222 governs operator visibility on it.

pricing_skus.unit_description: per /api/hdk/map/capabilities call (mobile app polls on resume)
